name.en: Bipolar Inventory of Signs and Symptoms Scale (BISS)

directions.en: Items are scored from 0 to 4, based on the most recent 7 day period, utilizing information from self report, and family and clinician observation both outside and during the interview. The anchor statements are examples of behaviors, proportions of time experiencing disturbance, severity of disturbance, and functional impairment that would qualify for a specific score, but do not exclude similar behaviors and internal feelings that would qualify for that score. Items are scored both on the basis of frequency and severity. A score of 3, in most cases, also entails behavior that is observable to others. A score of 0 means the symptom is completely absent. When in doubt between 2 ratings, assign the higher score. Some items in the mania section, e.g. No. 26, Hyperactive, rate behavior that may not have associated impairment of function or adverse consequences. For each defined item, please ask the bolded questions as they are written, or nearly so, for purposes of increasing the consistency of patient responses. The questions in italics are to be asked only if the patient indicates some symptomatology on the bolded general question(s) for the item. Additional questions to those in italics may be needed to establish item severity for individual patients. Rate each item independently. For example, a patient could have both psychomotor slowing (9) and agitation (22) if the behaviors occurred at different times over the rating period. When asking the questions for the item at the top of each page, start with the phrase, "Over the past week have..." The Scale lists depressive symptoms first. If the patient is known, or the primary problem area already identified, we recommend commencing the interview with the area of prominent symptomatology and concern to the patient, then completing all remaining sections.

note.en: Each item is rated 0 (absent) to 4 (severe) on the printed anchor set shown beside it; anchors are examples, not an exhaustive list, and when in doubt between two ratings the higher score is assigned.
note.hi: प्रत्येक आइटम छपाए हुए एंकर-समुच्चय के अनुसार 0 (अनुपस्थित) से 4 (गंभीर) तक रेट किया जाता है; एंकर उदाहरण हैं, पूर्ण सूची नहीं — दो रेटिंगों में संदेह हो तो उच्चतर अंक दें।

text.en: Sadness - reported: Subjective feeling of depression based on verbal complaints of feeling depressed, sad, blue, gloomy, down in the dumps, empty, "don't care." Do not include such ideational aspects as discouragement, pessimism, or worthlessness; suicide attempts or depressed appearance.

definition.en: Subjective feeling of depression based on verbal complaints of feeling depressed, sad, blue, gloomy, down in the dumps, empty, "don't care." Do not include such ideational aspects as discouragement, pessimism, or worthlessness; suicide attempts or depressed appearance.

probes.en: During the past 7 days, how have you been feeling? Describe your mood?
Have you felt depressed (sad, blue, moody, down, empty, as if you didn't care)?
Have you cried or been tearful? How often? Does it come and go? How long does it last? How bad is the feeling? Can you stand it?

anchors.en: Not at all
Slight; e.g., only occasionally feels "sad" or "down"
Mild; e.g., often feels somewhat "depressed," "blue" or "downhearted," and/or appears sad and is less responsive to positive stimulus
Moderate; e.g., most of the time feels "depressed," and/or several manifestations of sadness with limited ability to brighten up
Severe; e.g., most of the time feels "wretched," sustained gloomy appearance

text.en: Sadness - observed: Appears despondent, gloomy, despairing, as reflected in speech, facial expression, and posture. Rate also by inability to brighten up.

definition.en: Appears despondent, gloomy, despairing, as reflected in speech, facial expression, and posture. Rate also by inability to brighten up.

probes.en: Have others commented that you appeared sad, blue, or unhappy?

anchors.en: Not at all
Slight; e.g., looks dispirited, but brightens up easily
Mild; e.g., more physical manifestations of sadness, and less response to positive stimulus
Moderate; e.g., often appears sad and unhappy
Severe; e.g., extreme and continuous gloom and despondency

text.en: Pessimism: Discouragement, pessimism and hopelessness.

definition.en: Discouragement, pessimism and hopelessness.

probes.en: Have you been discouraged (pessimistic, felt hopeless)?
What kind of future do you see for yourself?
How do you think things will work out?
Can you see yourself or your situation getting any better?

anchors.en: Not at all
Slight; e.g., occasional feelings of discouragement about future
Mild; e.g., often somewhat discouraged
Moderate; e.g., very often feels quite pessimistic about the future
Severe; e.g., pervasive feelings of intense pessimism

text.en: Suicidality: Suicidal tendencies, including preoccupation with thoughts of death or suicide. Do not include mere fears of dying.

definition.en: Suicidal tendencies, including preoccupation with thoughts of death or suicide. Do not include mere fears of dying.

probes.en: When a person gets upset, depressed, or feels hopeless, he or she may think about dying or even killing themselves. Have you had any such thoughts?
Have you thought about how you would do it?
Have you told anybody about suicidal thoughts?
Have you actually done anything?

anchors.en: Not at all
Slight; e.g., occasional thoughts of death (without suicidal thoughts), "I would be better off dead" or "I wish I were dead."
Mild; e.g., frequent thoughts of being better off dead or occasional thoughts of suicide but has no plan or intent
Moderate; e.g. often thinks of suicide or has thought of a specific method
Severe; e.g. often thinks of suicide and has thought of a specific plan or has made a suicidal gesture or attempt

text.en: Worry: Worrying, brooding, painful preoccupation and inability to get mind off unpleasant thoughts (may or may not be accompanied by depressive mood).

definition.en: Worrying, brooding, painful preoccupation and inability to get mind off unpleasant thoughts (may or may not be accompanied by depressive mood).

probes.en: Have you been worrying a lot?
How much do you worry? What kinds of things have you been worrying about?
How much of your time is spent in this?
Are you able to get your mind off it?

anchors.en: Not at all
Slight; e.g., occasionally worries about some realistic or trivial problem
Mild; e.g., often worries excessively about a problem
Moderate; e.g., very often worries excessively about a realistic or trivial problem
Severe; e.g., most of the time is spent in worrying or brooding about problems which he/she cannot dispel

text.en: Guilt: Feelings of self-reproach or excessive, inappropriate guilt for things done or not done.

definition.en: Feelings of self-reproach or excessive, inappropriate guilt for things done or not done.

probes.en: Do you blame yourself for anything you have done or not done?
What about feeling guilty?
Do you feel you have done anything wrong?
Do you deserve punishment?
Do you feel you have brought this on yourself?
Have you been critical of yourself?

anchors.en: Not at all
Slight; e.g., occasional feelings of mild self-blame
Mild; e.g., often feels somewhat guilty about past actions, the significance of which are exaggerated, such as consequences of the illness
Moderate; e.g., often feels quite guilty about past actions or feelings of guilt that cannot be explained
Severe; e.g., pervasive feelings of intense guilt, self-reproach or generalizes feelings of self-blame

text.en: Feelings of inadequacy: Negative evaluation of him or herself, including feelings of inadequacy, failure, worthlessness.

definition.en: Negative evaluation of him or herself, including feelings of inadequacy, failure, worthlessness.

probes.en: How has your self-esteem been this past week?
Are you down on yourself?
What is your opinion of yourself compared to other people?
Worthless? A failure? How often do you feel this way about yourself?

anchors.en: Not at all
Slight; e.g., occasional feelings of inadequacy
Mild; e.g., often feels somewhat inadequate
Moderate; e.g., often feels like a failure
Severe; e.g., pervasive feelings of worthlessness

text.en: Low energy: Difficulty getting started, or slowness initiating and performing everyday activities. Subjective feeling of lack of energy or fatigue. Do not rate lack of interest.

definition.en: Difficulty getting started, or slowness initiating and performing everyday activities. Subjective feeling of lack of energy or fatigue. Do not rate lack of interest.

probes.en: Have you had less energy than usual to do things? Have you been getting tired easily? I am not talking about your interest in things, but your physical energy to do things.
Has this interfered with your accomplishing tasks that you ordinarily need to do? Have you needed help in getting started?

anchors.en: Not at all
Slight; e.g., occasional less energy than usual
Mild; e.g., at times definitely more tired, or less energy than usual
Moderate; e.g., most of time is very tired, lacking energy
Severe; e.g., spends most of time resting, nearly always feels fatigued

text.en: Psychomotor slowing: Generalized slowing down of physical reactions, movements, and speech, including latency in speech. Rate both on observed and reported information.

definition.en: Generalized slowing down of physical reactions, movements, and speech, including latency in speech. Rate both on observed and reported information.

probes.en: Have you been slowed down, not able to move as quickly as usual?
Did you find it hard to start talking?
Did you talk a lot less than usual?
Did you feel like you were moving in slow motion?

anchors.en: Not at all
Slight, of doubtful clinical significance, only subjective feeling of being slowed
Mild; e.g., conversation is noticeably retarded but not strained
Moderate; e.g., conversation is strained, or moves very slowly
Severe; e.g., conversation is difficult to maintain, or hardly moves at all

text.en: Loss of interest: Subjective experience of reduced interest in the surroundings, or activities that normally give pleasure. Reduced ability to react with adequate emotion to circumstances or people.

definition.en: Subjective experience of reduced interest in the surroundings, or activities that normally give pleasure. Reduced ability to react with adequate emotion to circumstances or people.

probes.en: When you participated in activities that you usually enjoy, were they pleasurable for you?
If you did not do any of your usual activities, was this because you did not have the opportunity? (If the answer is opportunity, do not rate towards loss of interest.)
Can you experience your usual feelings for your loved ones?

anchors.en: Not at all
Slightly reduced ability to enjoy usual interests. Reduced ability to feel anger
Mild; e.g., loss of interest in the surroundings/activities, loss of feelings for friends and acquaintances
Moderate; e.g., most of the time has moderately reduced interest in most pleasurable activities
Severe; e.g., feels emotionally paralyzed, inability to feel anger or grief, and a complete or even painful failure to feel for close relatives and friends

text.en: Social withdrawal: Reduced interest in and attention to others. Associated with reduced social interactions, and reduced time spent with others.

definition.en: Reduced interest in and attention to others. Associated with reduced social interactions, and reduced time spent with others.

probes.en: Have you had less interest in spending time with other people, including your family members, friends, or persons you work with?
Did you actually spend less time interacting with others?
How much less time than usual for you does this represent?
Did you avoid social contact with people whom you normally interact with?

anchors.en: Not at all
Slight reduction in interest in social interaction
Mild; e.g., actual reduction in social interaction, associated with some avoidance of others
Moderate; e.g., substantially reduced time spent with others, with some adverse consequences to the social avoidance
Marked reduction in social interactions, with consequent difficulties in relationships with family, friends, peers

text.en: Reduced sex drive: Reduced sexual interest, fantasies, or a reduction of sexual activity. Judge against the subject's usual sexual interests and habits when well.

definition.en: Reduced sexual interest, fantasies, or a reduction of sexual activity. Judge against the subject's usual sexual interests and habits when well.

probes.en: What has your sexual interest and activity been like this past week?
Has it been reduced at any time?
Can you tell me an example of the way it has changed, been low?

anchors.en: Not at all
Slight; sexual interest is reduced
Mild; e.g., definite reduction of sexual interest. Usual sexual activities partially reduced
Moderate; e.g., persistent reduction of sexual interest. Usual sexual activities reduced consistently
Severe; e.g., complete sexual indifference. "I have no interest in sex."

text.en: Anxiety - reported: Subjective feelings of anxiety, fearfulness, or apprehension, whether or not accompanied by somatic anxiety and whether focused on specific concerns or not.

definition.en: Subjective feelings of anxiety, fearfulness, or apprehension, whether or not accompanied by somatic anxiety and whether focused on specific concerns or not.

probes.en: Have you felt tense or anxious?
Does this get to the point that you feel uncomfortable?
Have you had anxiety attacks?
Are you able to control these feelings?

anchors.en: Not at all
Slight; e.g., fleeting inner tension
Mild; e.g., periods of tension, fear that can be mastered
Moderate; e.g., tense, ill at ease most of the time, minimal ability to control tension, fear
Severe; e.g., tense, fearful, frequent anxiety attacks. Often functionally incapacitating

text.en: Anxiety - observed: Autonomic over-activity and/or muscle tension, expressed in facial appearance, flushing, sweating, cold hands, posture, movements.

definition.en: Autonomic over-activity and/or muscle tension, expressed in facial appearance, flushing, sweating, cold hands, posture, movements.

probes.en: Over the past week have others commented that you appeared tense or showed signs of anxiety, such as sweating or clammy hands?

anchors.en: Not at all
Slight; occasional or slight autonomic disturbances such as flushing or sweating under stress
Mild; e.g., autonomic disturbance on several occasions, even when not under stress
Moderate; e.g., tense, ill at ease most of the time, minimal ability to control tension, fear
Severe; e.g., tense, fearful, frequent anxiety attacks. Often functionally incapacitating.

text.en: Somatic anxiety - reported: Has been bothered by 1 or more physiological concomitants of anxiety.

definition.en: Has been bothered by 1 or more physiological concomitants of anxiety.

probes.en: Have you been bothered by physical symptoms like palpitations, shortness of breath, sweating, headaches, stomach cramps, diarrhea or muscle tension?
If yes, determine if there were other symptoms and the overall severity of the disturbance.

anchors.en: Not at all
Slight; e.g., occasionally palms sweat excessively
Mild; e.g., often has 1 or more physical symptoms to a mild degree
Moderate; e.g., often has several symptoms or 1 symptom to a considerable degree
Severe; e.g., very frequently bothered by 1 or more symptoms or 1 symptom to a severe degree

text.en: Fearfulness: Alerting response associated with perceived unfamiliar or threatening sound, visualization, event or smell, coupled with autonomic arousal (increased pulse, heavy breathing), impulse to retreat or attack.

definition.en: Alerting response associated with perceived unfamiliar or threatening sound, visualization, event or smell, coupled with autonomic arousal (increased pulse, heavy breathing), impulse to retreat or attack.

probes.en: Some people feel frightened easily when unpleasant events take place around them. Has that happened to you in the past week?
What about feeling frightened unexpectedly?
Has the degree that you have been frightened been more than when you are feeling well?
How have you felt inside when this has happened?
How well have you been able to control the fear?

anchors.en: Not at all
Slight, occasional feelings of fear that quickly abate
Mild, e.g.; occasional fear that persists despite efforts to control
Moderate, e.g., fearful most days, sometimes associated with retreating or hostile reaction
Severe, e.g.; quite fearful most days, much of day. Unable to control fear, or at least one intensely fearful experience.

text.en: Insomnia: Sleep disturbance, including initial, middle and terminal difficulty in getting to sleep or staying asleep or waking up earlier than usual. Take into account the estimated number of hours slept and subjective sense of lost sleep. Do not rate decreased need for sleep.

definition.en: Sleep disturbance, including initial, middle and terminal difficulty in getting to sleep or staying asleep or waking up earlier than usual. Take into account the estimated number of hours slept and subjective sense of lost sleep. Do not rate decreased need for sleep.

probes.en: Are you taking any medication to help you sleep?
How has your sleep been this last week?
Did you have any difficulty getting to sleep? How many hours a night were you able to sleep even when tired?
How many days did you have difficulty sleeping?
How does that compare with a usual full night of sleep for you?

anchors.en: No experience of insomnia during rating period
Slight; e.g., occasional difficulty with insomnia.
Mild; e.g., often has some significant difficulty
Moderate; e.g., usually has considerable difficulty
Severe; e.g., almost always has great difficulty

text.en: Excessive sleep: Increased duration of sleep, compared to the subject's own normal pattern when well. The questions for item 17 will aid in rating this item. It is possible that a patient could receive a positive score for both item 17 and 18. Rate independent of whether person is taking a drug that might alter sleep.

definition.en: Increased duration of sleep, compared to the subject's own normal pattern when well. The questions for item 17 will aid in rating this item. It is possible that a patient could receive a positive score for both item 17 and 18. Rate independent of whether person is taking a drug that might alter sleep.

probes.en: During the past week, have you overslept in the morning?
Do you take naps during the day?
Do you ever have difficulty getting out of bed?
How many more hours sleep have you been getting than usual?

anchors.en: No excessive sleep during this period
Slight; sleeps longer than usual 1-2 nights/week
Mild; sleeps 2-3 hours extra most days
Moderate; e.g., spends part of day asleep in spite of normal or increased sleep at night
Severe; sleep increased by 4 or more hours, difficulty getting out of bed, despite excessive duration of sleep

text.en: Reduced appetite: Appetite compared to usual.

definition.en: Appetite compared to usual.

probes.en: Has your appetite for food changed in the last week compared to the way it usually is?
Have you eaten less than you usually do?
Do you have to force yourself to eat?
Do other people have to urge you to eat?
Over the past month, has your weight changed? By how much?

anchors.en: No change at all
Slight decrease, questionable clinical significance
Mild decrease in appetite
Moderate decrease in appetite associated with change in weight
Severe loss of appetite, e.g., no appetite, significant weight loss

text.en: Increased appetite: Increase in appetite and/or binge eating.

definition.en: Increase in appetite and/or binge eating.

probes.en: Have you eaten more than you usually do?
Are you able to control how much you eat?
Have you binged on any foods?
Have you eaten snacks between regular meals? Appetite associated with change in weight?
How much of the time have you binged, eaten snacks, etc?

anchors.en: Not at all
Slight increase, questionable clinical significance
Mild increase in appetite
Moderate loss of control over eating and/or increase in appetite associated with change in weight
Severe increase (loss of control over eating or significant weight gain)

text.en: Impaired concentration: Difficulty in collecting one's thoughts, mounting to incapacitating lack of concentration. Rate frequency, intensity and degree of incapacity produced.

definition.en: Difficulty in collecting one's thoughts, mounting to incapacitating lack of concentration. Rate frequency, intensity and degree of incapacity produced.

probes.en: How well have you been able to concentrate?
Are there any times when your concentration has been below your normal level?
Has this interfered with your reading, work, making conversation with others?

anchors.en: Not at all
Slight; e.g., occasional difficulties in collecting one's thoughts
Mild; e.g., difficulties in concentrating and sustaining thought, which at times interferes with reading or conversation
Moderate; e.g., most of time has impaired concentration, and usual responsibilities and actions are hampered by this
Severe; e.g., incapacitating lack of concentration

text.en: Agitation: Purposeless motor activity. Inability to sit still, pacing, fidgeting, wringing hands, pulling at clothes, movement of lips or fingers. Do not include feeling of tension or restlessness. Rate observed and reported behavior.

definition.en: Purposeless motor activity. Inability to sit still, pacing, fidgeting, wringing hands, pulling at clothes, movement of lips or fingers. Do not include feeling of tension or restlessness. Rate observed and reported behavior.

probes.en: Were there times when you were unable to sit still? Did you feel like you had to be constantly pacing up and down?
Did you notice that you were pulling on your clothing, hair, or skin? Did you wring your hands? How frequently did you do this? Did it cause you any difficulties in the way you functioned?

anchors.en: Not at all
Slight, and of doubtful clinical significance
Mild; e.g., occasionally fidgety or unable to sit quietly in a chair
Moderate; e.g., often pulling at hair, clothing, etc or having to move
Severe; e.g., constantly fidgety or pulling at hair, clothing, etc or pacing up and down

text.en: Irritability - reported: Subjective feeling of anger, resentment, or annoyance (directed externally) whether expressed overtly or not. Rate only the intensity and duration of the subjective sense of irritability.

definition.en: Subjective feeling of anger, resentment, or annoyance (directed externally) whether expressed overtly or not. Rate only the intensity and duration of the subjective sense of irritability.

probes.en: How irritated, angry, or resentful have you felt - whether you showed it or not?
How strongly did you feel this way? How much of the time did you feel this way? How did you show your (anger, annoyance, irritability)?

anchors.en: Not at all
Slight and of doubtful clinical significance
Mild; e.g., definitely more irritable than called for by the situation but only occasional and not intense
Moderate; e.g., often feelings quite angry or occasionally feels very angry
Severe; e.g., most of the time quite angry or often feels very angry

text.en: Irritability - observed: Overt expression of irritability, annoyance and anger. Do not rate subjective feelings of annoyance, anger, or irritability on this item, no matter how intense, unless it is expressed overtly. Include any irritability observed by others.

definition.en: Overt expression of irritability, annoyance and anger. Do not rate subjective feelings of annoyance, anger, or irritability on this item, no matter how intense, unless it is expressed overtly. Include any irritability observed by others.

probes.en: Over the past week, have you expressed your irritation or anger to others? How often did that occur?

anchors.en: Not at all
Slight and of doubtful clinical significance
Mild; e.g., definitely more irritable than called for by the situation but only occasional and not intense
Moderate; e.g., often displays anger
Severe; e.g., most of the time displays intense anger

text.en: Aggressive behavior: Confrontational, argumentative behavior.

definition.en: Confrontational, argumentative behavior.

probes.en: During the past week, have there been any times when you were loud, demanding, or sarcastic?
Did you have any arguments or confrontations with people?
Did you lose your temper when the above occurred? Did you throw or break anything? Did you push or hit anyone?

anchors.en: Not at all
Slight and of doubtful clinical significance
Mild; e.g., loud, sarcastic, at times, but only occasionally
Moderate; e.g., often demanding or loud
Severe; e.g., most of time somewhat demanding, loud, or any episode of shouting, hitting, breaking

text.en: Hyperactive: Increase in goal-directed activity as compared with usual level. Consider changes in involvement or activity level associated with work, family, friends, sex drive, projects, interests or activities (e.g., telephone calls, letter writing). Note that this item rates behaviour that may not have associated impairment of function or adverse consequences.

definition.en: Increase in goal-directed activity as compared with usual level. Consider changes in involvement or activity level associated with work, family, friends, sex drive, projects, interests or activities (e.g., telephone calls, letter writing). Note that this item rates behaviour that may not have associated impairment of function or adverse consequences.

probes.en: Have you been more active or involved in things than usual?
What about your work, housekeeping, family, friends, sex, hobbies, new projects or interests? How much of your day has been spent on this?

anchors.en: Not at all
Slightly more interest in activities, but of questionable significance
Mild increase in activity level
Moderate increase in activity
Marked increase, almost constantly involved in numerous activities in many areas

text.en: Energetic: Unusually energetic, more active than the usual level without expected fatigue.

definition.en: Unusually energetic, more active than the usual level without expected fatigue.

probes.en: Have you had more energy than usual to do things?
More than just a return to normal or usual level?
Did it seem like too much energy?

anchors.en: Not at all
Slightly more energetic but of questionable significance
Mild increase in energy. Less fatigued than usual.
Moderate increase in energy compared to usual, with little or no fatigue
Markedly more energetic than usual, all or nearly all of time, with little or no fatigue

text.en: Increased social interest: Increased interest in, attention to others. Associated with increased social interactions and time spent with others.

definition.en: Increased interest in, attention to others. Associated with increased social interactions and time spent with others.

probes.en: Have you had more interest than usual in spending time with other people, including church, family, friends, co-workers?
Did you actually spend more time interacting with others?
How much more time than usual for you does this represent?
Did you make social contact with people whom you do not know or have not seen in a long time? What about talking on the phone, or using the internet for conversations?

anchors.en: Not at all
Slight increase in interest in social interaction.
Mild; actual increase in social interaction, associated with actively seeking out others
Moderate; substantially increased time spent with others, causing minor impairment, e.g., inappropriate renewing of old acquaintances
Marked increase in social interactions, associated with intrusive, unwanted interactions, contacts strangers

text.en: Racing thoughts - reported: Rapid flow of ideas, which may be observable in speech. There is continuity of thought, although it may be difficult or impossible to stay on track with the content. Rate on subjective report.

definition.en: Rapid flow of ideas, which may be observable in speech. There is continuity of thought, although it may be difficult or impossible to stay on track with the content. Rate on subjective report.

probes.en: Have you been bothered by having too many thoughts at once?
Have your thoughts been speeded up?
Has this caused any difficulties in staying on track?
How much of the time has this happened? Is it moderate or severe over the past week?
How different was that from when you are feeling normal?

anchors.en: Not at all
Slight; e.g., feels talkative
Mild; e.g., free, lively associations, not interfering with person's staying on track
Moderate; e.g., rapid flow of ideas, with difficulty returning to primary theme of thoughts
Severe; e.g., constantly feels thoughts racing, has great difficulty collecting thoughts and returning to main focus

text.en: Pressured speech: Pressure of talk, increased flow of speech, overly loquacious. Rate both observed and reported behavior.

definition.en: Pressure of talk, increased flow of speech, overly loquacious. Rate both observed and reported behavior.

probes.en: Have you experienced yourself talking too fast, saying too much in conversations?
Did others have to interrupt to get a word in?
Has this interfered with your effectiveness in conversations?

anchors.en: Not at all
Slight; e.g., tendency to talk excessively, not impairing
Mild; e.g., rapid, verbose speech. Gives detailed answers
Moderate; e.g., garrulous, difficult to interrupt
Severe; e.g., speaking almost constantly. Words come tumbling out. Cannot be interrupted most of time.

text.en: Increased sexuality: Stronger sexual interest than usual. May be reflected in an increase in sexual activities or fantasies. Judge in comparison with subject's usual sexual habits when well.

definition.en: Stronger sexual interest than usual. May be reflected in an increase in sexual activities or fantasies. Judge in comparison with subject's usual sexual habits when well.

probes.en: How has your interest in sexual activities been the past week?
Have you thought about, or talked about sexual matters more than usual?
What has your level of sexual activity been?

anchors.en: Not at all
Slight increase in sexual interest
Mild increase in sexual interest, e.g., fantasies that at times preoccupy patient
Moderate; e.g., definite increase in sexual interest or activities, or intrusive sexual fantasies
Severe; e.g., preoccupied with sexual fantasies. Marked increase in sexual activities

text.en: Less need for sleep: Less need for sleep during the past week. A patient could be scored positive on this item as well as items 17 and 18 for impaired sleep.

definition.en: Less need for sleep during the past week. A patient could be scored positive on this item as well as items 17 and 18 for impaired sleep.

probes.en: Have you needed less sleep than usual to feel rested?
How many hours did you sleep? How many days in the last week did you have a reduced need for sleep? How much sleep do you ordinarily need?

anchors.en: No reduced need for sleep in past week
Slight; up to 1 hour less than usual
Mild; up to 2 hours less than usual
Moderate; up to 3 hours less than usual
Severe; 4 or more hours less than usual

text.en: Grandiose: Increased self-esteem and appraisal of his/her worth, contacts, power or knowledge (up to grandiose delusions) as compared with usual level. Persecutory delusions should not be considered evidence of grandiosity unless the subject feels the persecution is due to some special attributes of his/hers (e.g., power, contacts.)

definition.en: Increased self-esteem and appraisal of his/her worth, contacts, power or knowledge (up to grandiose delusions) as compared with usual level. Persecutory delusions should not be considered evidence of grandiosity unless the subject feels the persecution is due to some special attributes of his/hers (e.g., power, contacts.)

probes.en: Have you felt more self-confident than usual?
Have you felt that you are a particularly important person, or that you have special talents, abilities?
What about special plans?

anchors.en: Not at all
Slight; e.g., is more expansive, confident than most people in similar circumstances
Mild; e.g., definitely inflated self-esteem or exaggerates talents somewhat out of proportion to circumstances
Moderate; e.g., inflated self-esteem clearly out of proportion to circumstances
Severe; e.g., grandiosity also may have delusional component

text.en: Elated: Elevated mood and/or optimistic attitude toward the future, out of proportion to the circumstances.

definition.en: Elevated mood and/or optimistic attitude toward the future, out of proportion to the circumstances.

probes.en: Have there been times when you felt very good or too cheerful or high - not just your normal self?
Did you feel on top of the world or as if there was nothing you couldn't do?
Have you felt that everything would work out just the way you wanted?

anchors.en: Not at all
Slight; e.g., good spirits more cheerful than most people in similar circumstances, but of only doubtful clinical significance
Mild; e.g., definitely elevated mood and optimistic outlook that is somewhat out of proportion to the circumstances
Moderate; e.g., mood and outlook are clearly out of proportion to circumstances
Severe; e.g., quality of euphoric, exalted mood

text.en: Sharpened thinking: Has experienced unusually sharp and clear thinking, associated with creativity, problem solving capabilities.

definition.en: Has experienced unusually sharp and clear thinking, associated with creativity, problem solving capabilities.

probes.en: Have there been periods when your thinking seemed especially clear during the week?
Do you recall having had any unusually creative ideas or approaches to problems?

anchors.en: Not at all
Slight; e.g., brief periods of thinking more clearly or creatively
Mild increase in clarity or creativity of thought
Moderate increase; e.g., believes that has important insight into personal or external affairs but, with real evidence for this

Marked; e.g., most of time thinking seems exceptionally clear, creative, may be associated with some adverse consequence, e.g., acts on basis of belief in plans, but without reasonable chance of success in action taken

text.en: Elevated evening energy, interests: Increases in energy, activity, or interests in evening/night period.

definition.en: Increases in energy, activity, or interests in evening/night period.

probes.en: Has your energy, activity or interests been about the same throughout the day?
Have you had any tendency to be particularly active or take on projects in the evening or at night?
Have you had more energy during the evening or nighttime?
Have these kept you up past your usual hour of going to bed, or beyond midnight?
Has it ever been difficult to stop what you are doing, e.g., reading, TV, project at night?

anchors.en: Not at all
Slight; e.g., frequently has more energy, interests in evening that delay time of getting to bed by up to 1 hour

Mild; e.g., most evenings takes on activities that delay time getting to sleep by up to 2 hours, feels more energized most evenings/nights with difficulty calming down. Has difficulty discontinuing activities at night.
Moderate; e.g., definite impairment from increased diurnal energy, interests in evenings. Stays up, active beyond midnight. Sleep delayed by over 2 hours.
Severe; e.g., marked interference with time that sleep period starts, and interference with ordinary daytime activities due to elevated energy, activity, or interests in the evening/night

text.en: Impulsive: Makes decisions, starts actions without considering consequences. Impulsivity may be associated with intrusiveness, spending, criticism of others, sexual behavior.

definition.en: Makes decisions, starts actions without considering consequences. Impulsivity may be associated with intrusiveness, spending, criticism of others, sexual behavior.

probes.en: Have you made any decisions without thinking the situation through?
Have you made any snap judgments? Have you talked when you should have kept quiet or taken on a project without thinking it through?

Have you been able to control your responses when placed in a situation where a decision or choice is needed? Have you been patient or impatient when you have had to stand in line, say at a check out counter? Have you cut in line?
Have you bought things that you did not need?

anchors.en: Not at all
Slight; e.g., occasional impulsive action with little or no adverse consequences
Mild; e.g., frequent mildly impulsive actions with some adverse consequences, e.g., mild speeding, cutting in line
Moderate; e.g., frequent impulsive actions, with actual or realistic potential for adverse consequences such as firing, legal charge, traffic ticket. Impulsivity is evident during the interview
Severe; serious impairment from impulsivity; e.g., accident with medical consequences, ticketed by the police

text.en: Distractible: Attention easily diverted by external stimuli. Rate principally on observed behavior.

definition.en: Attention easily diverted by external stimuli. Rate principally on observed behavior.

probes.en: Do you notice that your attention shifts to other things taking place around you?
Have you been easily distracted by your surroundings?
Have you found this causing you to have difficulty in staying on a subject in conversation, or to concentrate?

anchors.en: Not at all
Slight; e.g., attention occasionally distracted by irrelevant stimuli, such as background noises
Mild; e.g., easily distracted, but returns to primary theme without prompting
Moderate; e.g., relatively frequent distraction, has difficulty getting back on track, even with prompting
Severe; e.g., continually distracted by incidental events and objects, which makes interviewing difficult

text.en: Risky behavior: Involvement in activities with high potential for adverse consequences socially, legally, financially or sexually.

definition.en: Involvement in activities with high potential for adverse consequences socially, legally, financially or sexually.

probes.en: Have you done anything that was risky or got you in trouble?

Have spent more than you can afford? Have you told someone off unnecessarily, driven too fast, or done any other things that could have gotten you into trouble? Have you used any drugs that could be harmful to you?
How often has this occurred over the past week? Can you give an example?

anchors.en: Not at all
Slight; e.g., thoughts of promiscuous behavior, moderately aggressive driving
Mild; e.g., places self in situations with some risk for injury, attention by police, contracting communicable disease
Moderate; e.g., frequent risk taking, with at least one serious risk taking action
Severe; e.g., argues with officials without provocation, runs red lights, solicits sex

text.en: Affective lability: Reported and observed spontaneous sharp shifts of affective or mood states lasting from minutes to hours. Lability may or may not be influenced by circumstances. Often described metaphorically: "I am on a roller coaster, I am like a yo yo." Affects can be sad, giddy, angry, or over confident. Do not rate on basis of what affective states are expressed. Rate on proportion of time with lability, degree of inability to control affective shifts.

definition.en: Reported and observed spontaneous sharp shifts of affective or mood states lasting from minutes to hours. Lability may or may not be influenced by circumstances. Often described metaphorically: "I am on a roller coaster, I am like a yo yo." Affects can be sad, giddy, angry, or over confident. Do not rate on basis of what affective states are expressed. Rate on proportion of time with lability, degree of inability to control affective shifts.

probes.en: How steady has your mood been?
Do your emotions shift fairly suddenly at times?
How much of the time are you this way? When this happens can you put a halt to it? Does it interfere in your daily life?

anchors.en: Not at all
Slight; e.g., occasional periods of fluctuating mood, affects, generally within a day, of questionable clinical significance
Mild; e.g., frequent mild, mood instability or lability which family, close associates see as dysfunctional
Moderate; e.g., definite impairment in social, work role function from frequent mood instability
Serious impairment from mood lability. Persists most of day, most days, interferes with most social, work, role functions

text.en: Persecutory ideas: From slight distrustfulness through suspiciousness and delusions of persecution. Does not include feelings or beliefs which are completely justified by the situation.

definition.en: From slight distrustfulness through suspiciousness and delusions of persecution. Does not include feelings or beliefs which are completely justified by the situation.

probes.en: Have people been making life hard or deliberately causing you trouble or trying to hurt you?
Have you had to be on guard with people?
Have you felt distrustful of others, or afraid that they would take advantage of you? Have you felt that you have been singled out, or targeted for their actions against you?

anchors.en: Not at all
Slight feelings of distrustfulness which may be realistically based and are of doubtful clinical significance
Mild; suspiciousness definitely not warranted by the situation, but only occasional and of mild intensity, e.g., often feels taken advantage of
Moderate; often suspicious or distrustful, but clearly ideas of reference that are recognized as the imagination
Severe; pervasive suspiciousness, or persecutory feelings of delusional intensity, e.g., plot may exist against him/her

text.en: Delusions: Severity of delusions of any type - consider conviction in delusion, preoccupation, and effect on actions. Ask questions appropriate to eliciting delusional ideation.

definition.en: Severity of delusions of any type - consider conviction in delusion, preoccupation, and effect on actions. Ask questions appropriate to eliciting delusional ideation.

probes.en: Has your imagination been playing tricks on you in any way?
Have you had any ideas that other people might not understand?
Did you think this was your imagination?
Have you felt controlled by an outside power?
What did you do about it?

anchors.en: Not at all
Slight; suspected or likely, but not impairing
Mild; delusion definitely present, but at times subject questions it as a false belief
Moderate; delusion has a significant effect on thoughts, feelings, actions, e.g., asks family to forgive sins, preoccupied with belief that he or she has special power.
Severe; delusions have major impact on patient or others, e.g., has delusions of control, calls emergency number about space invaders

text.en: Hallucinations: Severity of hallucinations of any type. Consider conviction in reality of hallucination, preoccupation, and effects on behaviors. Ask questions appropriate to eliciting hallucinations.

definition.en: Severity of hallucinations of any type. Consider conviction in reality of hallucination, preoccupation, and effects on behaviors. Ask questions appropriate to eliciting hallucinations.

probes.en: Have you heard voices or other things that weren't there or that other people couldn't hear?
Has there been anything unusual about the way things looked or sounded or smelled?
Do you think this was your imagination?
What did you do about it?

anchors.en: Not at all
Slight; occasional altered perception of doubtful clinical significance
Mild; definitely present, but is generally aware that it is imagination and is usually able to ignore it
Moderate; generally believes in the reality of the hallucination, but it has little influence on behavior
Severe; convinced the hallucination is real and it has significant effects on actions, e.g., locks doors to keep heard pursuers away

text.en: Impaired insight: Awareness, understanding of his/her emotional illness, aberrant behavior, and corresponding need for psychiatric treatments.

definition.en: Awareness, understanding of his/her emotional illness, aberrant behavior, and corresponding need for psychiatric treatments.

probes.en: Why are you coming for psychiatric treatment?
Do you feel that you currently have an emotional problem, or mental illness?
Do you believe that you need psychiatric treatment?
How would you explain your (behavior, symptoms, etc)?

anchors.en: Not at all; insight is present, patient admits, understands illness and need for treatment
Slight impairment; patient feels he/she is ill, or needs treatment, but has little insight into history of illness or what characterizes the illness.
Mild; admits behavior is changed, or need for treatment, but attributes it to a nonpsychiatric external factor (i.e., marital conflict, stress). Factors are plausible and non-delusional.
Moderate impairment; admits behavior is changed, or need for treatment, but gives implausible or delusional explanations
Severe; denies behavior change, illness, or need for treatment

rule.en: Section totals are the sum of the item scores: Depression items 1-20 (0-80) and Mania items 21-44 (0-96). An item counts as symptomatic at score >= 2 (mild or worse). The published use of the BISS is dimensional - severity of bipolar signs and symptoms over 7 days and change over time - it has no diagnostic cutoff, so no total converts into a diagnosis. Item 4 (suicidality) >= 1 and items 25/39/43 >= 2 require immediate clinical review.
rule.hi: विभाग-योग इतना है: अवसाद आइटम 1-20 (0-80) तथा उन्माद आइटम 21-44 (0-96)। स्कोर >= 2 पर आइटम लक्षणमान्य होता है। BISS का प्रकाशित प्रयोग विमात्मक (7 दिनों में द्विध्रुवी लक्षणों की तीव्रता एवं समय के साथ परिवर्तन) है — इसका कोई नैदानिक कटऑफ नहीं, अतः कुल अंक रोग-निर्णय नहीं बनाता। आइटम 4 >= 1 तथा 25/39/43 >= 2 पर तत्काल चिकित्सकीय समीक्षा आवश्यक।

interpretationNote.en: The BISS was designed to capture the full range of bipolar signs and symptoms rather than to generate a categorical diagnosis; interpret the depression and mania profiles together with the longitudinal course, collateral report and DSM-5/ICD criteria.
interpretationNote.hi: BISS वर्गीकृत रोग-निर्णय हेतु नहीं, द्विध्रुवी लक्षणों की सम्पूर्ण श्रेणी पकड़ने हेतु निर्मित है; अवसाद एवं उन्माद प्रोफाइल को दीर्घानुक्रमिक पाठ्यक्रम, सह-सूचना एवं DSM-5/ICD मानदंडों संग पढ़ें।

translationNote.en: Item text, probes and verbal anchors are the English original. Hindi is provided for the scale title only; the printed instrument is English-language and must be administered in English until a validated translation exists.
translationNote.hi: आइटम-पाठ, प्रश्न एवं एंकर अंग्रेज़ी मूल से हैं। हिन्दी केवल शीर्षक हेतु; छपा मापनी अंग्रेज़ी में ही प्रयोज्य जब तक मान्यताप्त अनुवाद उपलब्ध न हो।
